title: StockSmart Consignment Conditions — Placement, Title, Consumption Billing, Shrink and Withdrawal
content:
**Conditions governing consigned stock under the StockSmart Vendor-Managed Inventory Program**

**C1. Placement.** Consigned bins are allowed only on a tier whose consigned bins term is yes, and consigned stock is placed only while the program's consigned stock value stays at or below the tier's consigned value cap.

**C2. Title and billing.** Title to consigned stock passes to the customer under the tier's title transfer term when it is issued from the bin; issues during a calendar month are billed at the contract unit price in effect on the issue dates under the tier's consumption billing cycle, on one invoice dated the last day of the month together with that month's shrink.

**C3. One consumption bill a month.** Each program is billed at most once for a billing month's consumption.

**C4. Cycle counts and shrink.** At each cycle count, every cycle count interval of the tier in months, a shortage of consigned stock is absorbed by Corbett up to the tier's shrink tolerance percent of the consigned value counted; the shortage value above the tolerance is billed at the tier's shrink billing basis, allocated to the short items in descending order of their shortage value.

**C5. Slow movers and withdrawals.** At each par review a consigned item turning fewer than the tier's minimum annual turns times a year is withdrawn and converted to customer-owned replenishment; when a consigned bin is removed or the program ends, the stock still in it is withdrawn at no charge.

### The consigned stock value

The program's consigned stock value is the value, at contract unit price, of Corbett-owned consigned inventory in the customer's bins under the program: consignment stocking increases it; consumption billed, shrink billed and withdrawals decrease it.

### Shrink allocation — hypothetical example

A hypothetical cycle count values 20000.00 of consigned stock counted on a tier with a 1.0 percent tolerance and finds a shortage of 350.00: item P short 200.00, item Q short 150.00. Corbett absorbs 1.0 percent of 20000.00, that is 200.00; the 150.00 above the tolerance is billed and allocated to the short items in descending order of their shortage value, so it falls first on item P, whose 200.00 shortage covers it in full.

### Points of judgement

- C3 is read from the program's billing history: a billing month already carrying a consumption bill for that program carries no second one.
- Withdrawals on bin removal or program end carry no charge to the customer.
